newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fire blight said not in Australia apple/pear areas.
newsitem.headline: Fire blight said not in Australia apple/pear areas.

text.p: Fire blight bacterial disease was strongly believed to not exist in Australian apple and pear growing regions, the chief executive of the Australian Apple and Pear Growers' Association Jon Durham said in a statement.
The statement followed discovery of fire blight in the Botanic Gardens in Melbourne, Victoria, and the banning of movement of the fruit and nursery stock from Victria to other Australian states.
Pear and apple consumers had nothing to fear from the presence of the exotic disease in two plants in Melbourne's Botanic Gardens, Durham said.
Fire blight was not known to exist in any apple and pear growing region in Australia, he said.
Durham called on every Australian to eat at least five apples and two pears every week to assist the industry in its present crisis.
The Australian apple and pear industry has an estimated gross value of more than A$360 million.
